questions.question: In the dynamic lot-size model (demand $D_i$, order $y_i$, starting stock $x_i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i\ge0$, ordering cost $C_i(y_i)$ with $C_i(0)=0$, holding cost $h_i$ per unit of ending stock), the forward recursion uses values $f_i(x_{i+1})$ for each ending stock $x_{i+1}$ of period $i$. What does $f_i(x_{i+1})$ measure?
options: The least cost of periods $i+1,\dots,n$ when period $i+1$ starts with $x_{i+1}$
The least cost through period $i$ when period $i$ starts with stock $x_{i+1}$
The cost of period $i$ alone, its order plus holding the stock $x_{i+1}$
The least cost of periods $1,\dots,i$, holding included, ending with $x_{i+1}$

questions.question: In the dynamic lot-size model (demand $D_i$, order $y_i$, starting stock $x_i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i\ge0$, ordering cost $C_i(y_i)$ with $C_i(0)=0$, holding cost $h_i$ per unit of ending stock), with given initial stock $x_1$, the first stage is $f_1(x_2)=C_1(D_1+x_2-x_1)+h_1x_2$, with no minimum taken. Why is there no choice to make in period 1?
options: The order $y_1$ is chosen later, once $f_2$ is being computed
Given $x_1$, $D_1$ and $x_2$, the order must be $D_1+x_2-x_1$
Period 1 always orders exactly its own period demand $D_1$
Period 1 has no setup cost, so any order costs the same

questions.question: In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{0\le y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ ($D_i$ demand, $y_i$ order, $x_{i+1}$ ending stock, $C_i$ ordering cost with $C_i(0)=0$, $h_i$ holding cost). Why is the order $y_i$ restricted to $y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}$?
options: It caps $y_i$ at the production capacity of period $i$
It stops the order $y_i$ from ever exceeding the demand $D_i$
It keeps the starting stock $x_i$ of period $i$ nonnegative
It avoids holding costs on stock carried past period $i$

questions.question: In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{0\le y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ ($D_i$ demand, $y_i$ order, $x_{i+1}$ ending stock, $C_i$ ordering cost with $C_i(0)=0$, $h_i$ holding cost). Why can the recursion not simply take, in each period, the $y_i$ that makes $C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}$ smallest?
options: $y_i$ also fixes $x_i$, and thereby the earlier cost $f_{i-1}(x_i)$
That stage cost is the same for every $y_i$, so it cannot pick one
The cheapest choice is always $y_i=D_i$, which is rarely optimal
Holding costs are only charged at the end of the final period $n$

questions.question: In the dynamic lot-size model (demand $D_i$, order $y_i$, starting stock $x_i$, $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i\ge0$, ordering cost $C_i(y_i)$ with $C_i(0)=0$, holding cost $h_i$ per unit of ending stock), the forward recursion computes $f_n(x_{n+1})$ for the last period $n$, and the plan must end with no stock, $x_{n+1}=0$. Which value is the optimal total cost?
options: $\min_{x}f_n(x)$, the cheapest ending stock of period $n$
$f_n(0)$, the least cost through period $n$ ending at zero
$f_1(0)$, the cost of the first stage with zero ending stock
$f_1+f_2+\dots+f_n$, adding the values of all stages

questions.question: A lot-size model starts with stock $x_1=0$. Period 1 has demand $D_1=3$, setup cost $K_1=10$, unit cost 2 and holding cost $h_1=1$ per unit of ending stock. Using $f_1(x_2)=C_1(D_1+x_2-x_1)+h_1x_2$ with $C_1(y)=K_1+2y$ for $y>0$, what is $f_1(2)$?

Four units are on hand before period 1, where 3 units are demanded. Ordering costs $C_1(0)=0$ and $C_1(y)=10+2y$ for $y>0$, and each unit left at the end of period 1 costs $h_1=1$. With $f_1(x_2)=C_1(D_1+x_2-x_1)+h_1x_2$, what is the value for ending stock 1?
options: $+\infty$

questions.question: In the lot-size recursion the state is the ending stock $x_{i+1}$ and the starting stock follows from the balance $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$. Period $i$ has demand $D_i=3$, the order is $y_i=2$ and the ending stock is $x_{i+1}=1$. Which predecessor stock $x_i$ does the recursion look up in $f_{i-1}$?

In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{y_i}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ the predecessor stock $x_i=x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i$ must be nonnegative and $y_i\ge0$. For $D_i=2$ and $x_{i+1}=1$, which orders $y_i$ are compared?
options: $3$ only

questions.question: In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{0\le y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ ($D_i$ demand, $y_i$ order, $x_{i+1}$ ending stock, $C_i$ ordering cost with $C_i(0)=0$, $h_i$ holding cost). Several different order plans for periods $1,\dots,i$ end with the same stock $x_{i+1}$. Why may the recursion keep only the cheapest of them?
options: The cheapest plan has the fewest orders, which also suits later periods
Later periods favour the plan with the cheapest period-$i$ cost
Later periods see the past only through the ending stock $x_{i+1}$
Only the cheapest state of period $i$ is ever used by later periods

questions.question: In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{0\le y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ ($D_i$ demand, $y_i$ order, $x_{i+1}$ ending stock, $C_i$ ordering cost with $C_i(0)=0$, $h_i$ holding cost). Why does this recursion need far fewer cost evaluations than listing every complete order plan?
options: It considers only plans with $y_i=D_i$ in every period
It postpones every holding cost $h_ix_{i+1}$ to the last period $n$
It stops at the first plan that reaches $x_{n+1}=0$
It reuses each $f_{i-1}(x)$ for all routes through state $x$

questions.question: In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{0\le y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ ($D_i$ demand, $y_i$ order, $x_{i+1}$ ending stock, $C_i$ ordering cost with $C_i(0)=0$, $h_i$ holding cost). A predecessor stock that cannot be reached (it would need a negative order) gets $f_{i-1}=+\infty$. Why $+\infty$ rather than 0?
options: So that no decision leading to that state can ever be the minimum
Because the cost of such a state is too large to compute exactly
So that the state is penalized by a setup cost when it is used
Because unreachable states must be removed before period $i$ starts

questions.question: A three-period lot-size problem has demands $(D_1,D_2,D_3)=(3,2,2)$ and $x_1=0$, $x_4=0$. The recursion stored the best orders $y_3(0)=0$; $y_2(x_3)=2,3,4$ for $x_3=0,1,2$; $y_1(x_2)=3,4,5,7$ for $x_2=0,1,2,4$. Using $x_i=x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i$ backward, what is the optimal plan $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$?

A four-period lot-size problem has demands $(D_1,D_2,D_3,D_4)=(2,3,1,4)$ and must end with $x_5=0$. In the table of $f_2(x_3)$, the state $x_3$ is the stock carried from period 2 into period 3. What is the largest $x_3$ that can lie on an optimal plan?

In a lot-size recursion $f_1(0)=12$, $f_1(1)=15$, $f_1(2)=19$ (holding included). Period 2 has demand $D_2=2$, $C_2(0)=0$, $C_2(y)=8+2y$ for $y>0$ and $h_2=1$, and $f_2(x_3)=\min_{0\le y_2\le D_2+x_3}\{C_2(y_2)+h_2x_3+f_1(x_3+D_2-y_2)\}$. What is $f_2(0)$?

In the lot-size recursion $f_i(x_{i+1})=\min_{0\le y_i\le D_i+x_{i+1}}\{C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}+f_{i-1}(x_{i+1}+D_i-y_i)\}$ ($D_i$ demand, $y_i$ order, $x_{i+1}$ ending stock, $C_i$ ordering cost with $C_i(0)=0$, $h_i$ holding cost). Which change to the cost data would make the stock $x_{i+1}$ alone an insufficient state for this recursion?
options: A setup cost $K_i$ that is cheaper if period $i-1$ ordered
Demand $D_i$ that differs strongly from one period to the next
A variable cost $c_i(y_i)$ that is nonlinear in the batch size
Holding costs $h_i$ that change from one period to the next

questions.question: A lot-size problem starts with $x_1=3$; demands are $D_1=1$, $D_2=2$; each period has $C_i(0)=0$, $C_i(y)=5+y$ for $y>0$; $h_1=5$ and $x_3=0$. With $f_1(x_2)=C_1(D_1+x_2-x_1)+h_1x_2$ ($+\infty$ for a negative order) and $f_2(0)=\min_{y_2}\{C_2(y_2)+f_1(2-y_2)\}$, what is $f_2(0)$?
